summary: LAPD detective Mark Fuhrman, whose taped racist boasts and role in founding an anti-women clique inside the department undermined the 1995 O. J. Simpson prosecution, was convicted of perjury in 1996 and reinvented himself as a true-crime author and Fox pundit.

evidence.note: enlists in the Marines in 1970, serves offshore in the Vietnam era, later lies about combat
joins the LAPD in 1975, then the East LA TRASH/CRASH gang unit from 1977
fakes violent urges and combat history to win a stress disability pension; denied 1983
screenwriter tapes him from 1985 to 1994 boasting of brutality and using slurs
Men Against Women clique harassing female officers; 1997 LAPD report confirms it
June 1994 murders; he finds the glove and testifies, tapes surface at trial
pleads no contest to perjury in 1996 and moves to Sandpoint, Idaho; main span ends
true-crime author career: Moxley murder book and the Skakel prosecution
Fox News crime analyst, chokehold advocacy, death from throat cancer at 74

notes: Death year 2026 taken from the episode framing (recent death, age 74). main_span 1985-1996 runs from the taped interviews and Men Against Women to the perjury plea; the 1975 LAPD start is an alternative. Men Against Women was an informal clique, typed as police for lack of a better org_type. Washington, Idaho and Connecticut also appear but California dominates, hence US-CA.
